source.title: Open problems on graph eigenvalues studied with AutoGraphiX

accepted.question_text: For each integer n >= 10, is the connected graph on n vertices that maximizes the irregularity Irr(G) = lambda_1(G) - d_bar(G) always a pineapple graph PA(n,q), where PA(n,q) is the graph formed by a clique of size q together with n-q additional vertices that are pairwise nonadjacent and each adjacent to one common vertex of the clique, with q = floor(n/2) + 1? Equivalently, does every connected n-vertex graph satisfy Irr(G) <= Irr(PA(n, floor(n/2)+1)) for n >= 10?

evidence.quote: The problem of finding an upper bound on the irregularity and characterizing the most irregular graphs remains open.
Conjecture 2.1 The most irregular connected graph on n (n >= 10) vertices is a pineapple PA(n, q) in which the clique size q is equal to floor(n/2) + 1.

accepted.question_text: Let s(G) = lambda_1(G) - lambda_n(G) be the spectral spread of a connected graph G on n >= 3 vertices. Is it true that s(G) <= sqrt(4qn - 3q^2 - 2q + 1), where q = ceil(2n/3), with equality if and only if G is the complete split graph CS(n,q), meaning the graph whose vertex set is partitioned into a clique of size q and an independent set of size n-q = floor(n/3), with every clique vertex adjacent to every independent-set vertex?

evidence.quote: The problem of finding the maximum value of s(G) among the class of connected graphs of given order n is an open problem.

Conjecture 3.1' Let G be a connected graph on n >= 3 vertices. Then s(G) <= sqrt(4qn - 3q^2 - 2q + 1) with equality if and only if G is the complete split graph CS(n, q) with an independent set of size n - q = floor(n/3) and a clique of size q = ceil(2n/3).

accepted.question_text: For every simple graph G on n vertices, does the Nordhaus-Gaddum sum of adjacency spectral radii satisfy lambda_1(G) + lambda_1(G_complement) <= 4n/3 - 5/3 - f(n), where f(n) = (3n - 2 - sqrt(9n^2 - 12n + 12))/6 when n mod 3 = 1, f(n) = 0 when n mod 3 = 2, and f(n) = (3n - 1 - sqrt(9n^2 - 6n + 9))/6 when n mod 3 = 0? If equality holds, must either G or its complement be a complete split graph whose independent set has size ceil(n/3), and also floor(n/3) when n mod 3 = 2?

evidence.quote: Finding an upper bound of Nordhaus-Gaddum type on the index over the class of connected graphs on n vertices, our third problem, was independently posed by Nosal (1970) and by Amin and Hakimi (1972). More than 40 years later, the problem remains open

Conjecture 4.1 (Aouchiche et al. 2008a;Aouchiche and Hansen 2012) For any simple graph G, with complement G, index lambda_1(G) and n vertices we have lambda_1(G) + lambda_1(G) <= 4/3 n - 5/3 - ... This bound is sharp and attained if and only if G or G is a complete split graph with an independent set on ceil(n/3) vertices (and also on floor(n/3) vertices if n mod(3) = 2).

accepted.question_text: Among all unicyclic graphs on n vertices, which graph has maximum energy E(G), defined as the sum of the absolute values of the adjacency eigenvalues? More specifically, is the maximum attained by the cycle C_n when n <= 7 and n is not 4, and also when n = 9, 10, 11, 13, or 15; by Lol_4,3 when n = 4; and by the lollipop graph Lol_n,6 for all other n, where Lol_n,g is formed by joining a cycle C_g to a path P_(n-g) by a single edge between a cycle vertex and a path endpoint?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.2 Among unicyclic graphs on n vertices the cycle Cn has maximal energy if n <= 7 and n = 9, 10, 11, 13 and 15. For all other values of n the unicyclic graph with maximum energy is the lollipop Loln,6.

Theorem 5.5 Among all unicyclic graphs on n vertices, the cycle Cn has maximal energy if n <= 7 but n != 4, and n = 9, 10, 11, 13 and 15; Lol4,3 has maximal energy if n = 4. For all other values of n, the unicyclic graph with maximal energy is Loln,6.

accepted.question_text: For n = 14 and for all n >= 16, is the bicyclic molecular graph on n vertices with maximal energy the graph P_n^{6;6}, obtained from two 6-cycles and a path P_(n-12) by attaching each path endpoint to one of the cycles by a single edge? Here a molecular graph means a connected graph of maximum degree at most 4.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.9 For n = 14 and n >= 16, the bicyclic molecular graph of order n with maximal energy is the molecular graph of the alpha, beta diphenyl-polyene C6H5(CH)n-12C6H5, which is represented by the graph P6;6_n obtained from two copies of the cycle C6 and a path Pn-12 by attaching with an edge each endpoint of the path to on cycle (see Fig. 6).

The complete solution, in that case, was given by Huo et al. (2011). Theorem 5.10 Let G be any connected, bipartite bicyclic graph on n >= 12 vertices. Then E(G) <= E(P6;6_n) with equality if and only if G ≡ P6;6_n.

accepted.question_text: For every tricyclic graph G on n vertices with n = 20 or n >= 22, is the energy E(G) at most E(P_n^{6,6;6}), where P_n^{6,6;6} is the graph formed from three copies of C_6 and a path P_(n-18) by joining two of the 6-cycles to one endpoint of the path and the third 6-cycle to the other endpoint, one edge per attachment? Must equality occur only for G isomorphic to P_n^{6,6;6}?

evidence.quote: The problem of finding the tricyclic graphs maximizing the energy remains open.
Conjecture 5.11 Let G be a tricyclic graph on n vertices with n = 20 or n >= 22. Then E(G) <= E(P6,6;6_n) with equality if and only if G ≡ P6,6;6_n.

accepted.question_text: For every tetracyclic graph G on n >= 26 vertices, is the energy E(G) at most E(P_n^{6,6;6,6}), where P_n^{6,6;6,6} is the graph formed from four copies of C_6 and a path P_(n-24) by joining two of the 6-cycles to one endpoint of the path and the other two 6-cycles to the other endpoint, one edge per attachment? Must equality occur only for G isomorphic to P_n^{6,6;6,6}?

evidence.quote: The problem of finding the quadricyclic (also called tetracyclic) graphs maximizing the energy remains open.
Conjecture 5.12 Let G be a tetracyclic graph on n vertices with n >= 26. Then E(G) <= E(P6,6;6,6_n) with equality if and only if G ≡ P6,6;6,6_n.

accepted.question_text: Let r and n be positive integers with n >= 6r + 4, and let p = floor(r/2) and q = ceil(r/2). If P_n^{p×6;q×6} denotes the graph obtained from r copies of C_6 and a path P_(n-6r) with endpoints u and v by joining u to one vertex in each of p of the 6-cycles and v to one vertex in each of the remaining q 6-cycles, one edge per attachment, does every connected r-cyclic graph G on n vertices satisfy E(G) <= E(P_n^{p×6;q×6})? Must equality occur only when G is isomorphic to P_n^{p×6;q×6}?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.13 Let r and n be positive integers such that n >= 6r + 4. Then E(G) <= E(P^p×6;q×6_n), where p = floor(r/2) and q = ceil(r/2), with equality if and only if G ≡ P^p×6;q×6_n.
